why: Rule 1: p4 shows seg 9004 rising monotonically over its last 5 cm to 150k at 9001 (continuing into the 4.6 cm 175k stub to 9003), a genuine Bragg, so 9001/9003 is the stopping end and 9000 is the cool end everything points away from; every rival candidate is a 0-prong sub-cm blob with no dQ/dx opinion.

p4 shows 154 cm of flat MIP with no Bragg at either end, so the 1.33x rule-1 ratio carries no real signal and this is a near-tie; I break it with rule 2, taking the lower-z end 15001 (z=359) over 15000 (z=501).

Rule 1 at the deg-2 junction: the 36 cm track's dQ/dx rises away and peaks near 6001, the 3.6 cm 212k e/cm proton stub stops at 6000 pointing +z, and the shower debris (33003/35007/37011/36009) lies off 6013 toward +x; the prong pair opens at 111 deg so the collinearity trap does not apply.

Deg-4 junction where p4 shows seg 8001 as a textbook monotone stopping-proton profile falling from 247k at 8000 back to MIP at 8002, the 34.5 cm shower runs away to 8001, and three satellite blob pairs sit within 15 cm.

p4 shows the 16.5 cm segment rising over its last 4 cm to 175k at 2001 along the stopping template, so 2001 is the stopping end; rule 1 leaves 2000 as the start, and the two satellite dots lie further +z as rule 2 would expect.

p4 shows 100 cm of flat MIP with no Bragg at either end, so the 1.31x reading at 13001 is vertex-region charge rather than a stop; 13001 is ringed by five separate sub-cm hadronic blobs from 5 to 40 cm away while nothing sits at the other end.

Rule 1 textbook, confirmed on p4: the 7.1 cm pi+ climbs monotonically to 215k at 19004 and the 44 cm proton falls monotonically from 235k at 19005 along the proton template, so both stop away from 19003, with a MIP muon as the third prong.

p4 shows seg 15002 rising monotonically over its last 8 cm to 210k at 15001, tracking the stopping-muon template, so 15001 is the stop and rule 1 leaves 15002, which also carries a 2.4 cm stub and blob 61005 5 cm away.

Rule 3: p4 shows the 228 cm muon falling from 185k right at 2000 along the stopping template, and two Michel-like blobs (19002, 20004) sit on that same end, so 2000 is the far end and the MIP end 2001 at z=244 is the vertex.

The two-Bragg-ends trap resolved on p4: 9004 carries the 199 cm muon's genuine Bragg plus a 6.5 cm Michel, while the 6.7 cm proton beside 9001 climbs monotonically to 285k as it runs away from 9001, which is also ringed by four sub-cm blobs.

Deg-2 junction opening at 105 deg, far too wide for the collinearity trap, with a 24 cm heavily-ionising 2.8x MIP proton on one prong and a MIP muon on the other; it is also the lowest-z point of the cluster.

p4 kills the apparent Bragg at 8002 - the 97k mean is one 155k spike, not a monotone rise - while the track sits at MIP near 8001, so it starts there, and the 7.8 cm shower fragment falls monotonically from 87k at 8001 to 2k, marking a shower apex at the same point.

The 357 cm spine is one straight track (successive segment directions agree to 2.6 and 4.5 deg, so the collinearity trap disqualifies 17010/17004/17006, and p4 shows 17004's 96k is a delta spike that falls back to 30k); the far end 17003 has the real Bragg plus an 8.3 cm Michel, leaving the MIP start 17001.

Rule 1 fully satisfied at the deg-3 vertex and confirmed on p4: the 114 cm proton falls monotonically from 235k at 22000 along the proton template and the 64 cm pi+ climbs to 120k at 22003, so both stop away from 22001, which is also the lowest-z junction.

p4 shows the 158 cm muon falling from 148k right at the 14000 end along the stopping template, so that end is the stop; 14001 is the MIP start and sits amid a hadronic spray including a 285k e/cm proton blob 31 cm off.
